To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corneal, skin, kidney and heart cells of the Wistar-Furh inbred strain are equally potent in stimulating allogeneic Fisher rat lymphocytes.

the relative capacity of cornea, heart, kidney, and skin to stimulate allogenic lymphocytes is equal, and that there is a lack of differences in density of histocompatiblity antigens on the surface of corneal and other tissue cells.
corneal cells do not express more MHC antigens than other cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to determine the relative capacity of various tissues and cells of different origin to stimulate lymphocyte responses.
a comparison of the stimulatory capacity in allogeneic mixed culture of corneal and other tissues.
the relative stimulatory capacity of cornea, skin, heart and kidney cells in mixed culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corneal cells do not differ from other cells of the body with respect to the expression of Ag-B2 antigens.
corneal cells are not antigenically inert and that they do not differ in their capacity to stimulate allogenic lymphocytes from the other tissues studied.
the cornea is a normal tissue which expresses the same histocompatibility antigents as do the other tissues tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the corneal cells are not different from other tissue cells in the ability to induce an allogeneic immune response in vitro.
the density of histoincompatible Ag-B2 antigenic sites on the surface of the corneal epithelial cells of Wistar-Furt rats is the same as on heart, kidney and other cells.
the corneal epithelium is not an immunological privileged tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cornea is a very good source for the isolation and culture of corneal epithelial cells.
corneal cells can be used to study the role of histocompatibility Ags in allogeneic responses.
corneal cells have a stimulatory capacity similar to that of skin, kidney and heart cells.
